newsitem.title: USA: Body of a second Arizona flood victim is found.
newsitem.headline: Body of a second Arizona flood victim is found.

text.p: Rescuers on Thursday found a second body in a narrow canyon in northern Arizona where nine other hikers were believed to have been swept to their deaths by a flash flood.

The 11 hikers, most of them Europeans, were caught by an 11-foot (3.3-metre) wall of water that surged without warning through the picturesque Antelope Canyon on Tuesday as they photographed its spectacular red-and-orange sandstone cliffs.

"I'm going to assume we're looking for victims rather than survivors at this point," Sgt. Tom Florman of the Coconino County Sheriff's Department said. "It's just been too long (since the group was swept away)."

Rescuers recovered the body of a woman hiker on Wednesday, but hours of searching and digging on Thursday revealed only one more body, which was not immediately recovered from the winding slot canyon. It is so narrow in places that hikers must squeeze between the walls to get through.
Officials said the bodies of the other hikers could be buried under several feet of sand and silt left by the deadly floodwaters.

Rescuers were also searching the shores of Lake Powell, a popular boating area four miles (6.4 km) downstream from the site of the accident. "Some of the bodies could have been carried clear into the lake," Florman said.
About 55 people aided by specially trained dogs scoured the area, which is close to the border with Utah and about 50 miles (80 km) northeast of the Grand Canyon, by boat and helicopter and on foot.
The search was called off temporarily in the early afternoon of Thursday when a weather advisory warned of thunderstorms that might bring another flood, but it was resumed when the danger passed.

The 11 hikers consisted of seven from France, two from the United States, and one each from Britain and Sweden. Five of the hikers were on a tour organized by TrekAmerica, a Los Angeles-based company specializing in organizing hiking tours for Europeans.
TrekAmerica tour guide Poncho Quintana, 28, found by sheriff's deputies clinging to a cliff at the bottom of the narrow canyon on Tuesday, is believed to have been the lone survivor.
He told TrekAmerica executive Jack Aakhus just hours after the rescue, "The water just hit me, and it just kept coming." He was bruised and battered but not seriously injured, Aakhus said.

Northern Arizona has had several flash floods in recent days. Tourists and residents were evacuated from the Havasupai Indian Reservation near the Grand Canyon earlier this week because of flooding, and floods were blamed for an Amtrak passenger train derailment on Saturday.
